title: Lane Johnson: From OU Tight End to Two-Time Super Bowl Champion
question: Which former Oklahoma Sooner won two Super Bowls with the Philadelphia Eagles?
answer: Right tackle Lane Johnson (OU 2009-12) won Super Bowl LII and Super Bowl LIX with Philadelphia. The 2013 No. 4 overall pick made six Pro Bowls over 14 seasons, all with the Eagles, before announcing his retirement in October 2026.
summary: Lane Johnson went from Kilgore College QB and OU tight end to a two-time Super Bowl champion right tackle for the Eagles. Here is his unlikely path.
body: Few NFL linemen have a stranger origin story than Lane Johnson. Before he was an anchor on the Eagles' offensive line, he was a quarterback at Kilgore College in Texas, and as a teenager he once worked as a grave digger.

Johnson's Oklahoma years (2009-12) were a tour of the depth chart. He transferred in as a tight end and redshirted in 2009, played tight end and defensive end in 2010, moved to right tackle in 2011 and slid over to left tackle as a senior in 2012. That athletic, position-hopping résumé helped make him the No. 4 overall pick of the Philadelphia Eagles in 2013.

Philadelphia never let him go. Johnson spent all 14 of his NFL seasons with the Eagles, became a six-time Pro Bowler (2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2024) and earned five Associated Press All-Pro selections, two of them on the first team. He helped the club win three NFC championships, after the 2017, 2022 and 2024 seasons.

Most importantly, he owns two rings. Johnson was the Eagles' right tackle on the team that won Super Bowl LII and again on the team that won Super Bowl LIX, the only two Super Bowl titles in franchise history.
Johnson announced his retirement on Oct. 6, 2026, at age 36, closing one of the finest careers by a former Sooner offensive lineman.
